pr_body:
Pass `{safe: true}` to cssnano by default, to avoid the dangers of the advanced transforms that it would enable by default in cssnano@3.x

Adds a test (well co-opts an existing test) to ensure that @font-face files make it through to the final css bundle when `{ production: true }`

Once cssnano v4 is finally released as stable, the default options can be removed, as cssnano 4 will default to safe transforms only.

Fix #698

issue_context.title: @font-face files omitted when building with parcel build index.html
comments: I'm having this issue even when the @font-faces are included in a file with another CSS. They are just getting completely eaten from the output.
I'm seeing this too. Is it possible to alter parcels cssnano config? It feels like it's related to http://cssnano.co/optimisations/discardunused/

From parcel is currently using cssnano 3.10, and from the readme for that version:

> Note that cssnano enables aggressive optimisations by default, which might not always be what you want. Set options.safe to true if you want to disable this. In future versions, only safe options will be enabled by default, starting from version 4.
You can use `cssnano.config.js` to configure cssnano

@DeMoorJasper Could you share an example? I'm just scraping around the internet trying to find documentation, and it looks like it's a cssnano.config.js [was to be a cssnano v4](https://github.com/ben-eb/cssnano/issues/91) thing and parcel's [package.json on master](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/master/package.json#L23) is pointing at cssnano@3.10

Would it make sense to preemptively apply the cssnano 4 safe defaults behavior to Parcel (to avoid breaking things for new users)?

I don't think detecting whether or not this is harmful is feasible due to the prevalence of CSS-in-JS methods.
If it fixes the issue, it's probably a good idea. Def as it'll be the default in cssnano v4 anyway

review_comments:
Maybe change this to Object.assign(...)?
So config doesn't overwrite defaults but appends them

That's reasonable, but how would we communicate the net result to users. I think it's easier to reason about if we just use the `cssnano.config.js` as provided (_advanced user, let them choose_), and otherwise, just use safe defaults.
